prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance forward, puts the right elbow: or the right arm: in under uke's right armpit, overlaps with uke, and, using the extension of both arms and both knees, throws uke over the right shoulder.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall) From kumi-kata, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki and throws uke over the shoulder; uke lands taking ukemi. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) to break uke's balance forward, and throws uke forward over the shoulder. Cooperation of uke: So that tori does not bend forward, uke arches the upper body moderately even when lifted. How to take the ukemi: In time with tori's seoi-nage, uke does not pull the hips back and takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall).

Tori throws uke forward without lifting uke off the mat. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) and throws uke forward without lifting uke up. How to take the ukemi: Uke rotates sideways about the right foot and takes yoko-ukemi (side breakfall).
Two students practise the body movement together. Practise the tai-sabaki (body movement) in pairs.

As uke comes forward, tori turns in with ushiro-mawari-sabaki and applies the technique. Apply the technique with ushiro-mawari-sabaki (backward turning body movement) at the moment uke comes forward.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori should not push the hips in too deeply.
Tori must not apply the technique from a low posture, such as with both knees on the mat.
